statement: Define a cell to be a pair (i,j) with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n. Define a legal move as either ((i,j),(i,k)) with j < k < n and k - j <= grid[i][j], or ((i,j),(k,j)) with i < k < m and k - i <= grid[i][j]. Define a path as a finite sequence of cells (i_0,j_0),...,(i_t,j_t) with t >= 0, (i_0,j_0) = (0,0), (i_t,j_t) = (m-1,n-1), such that every consecutive pair is a legal move; its visited-cell count is t+1. The function returns a result r and: if at least one such path exists, then r is the minimum visited-cell count over all such paths; if no such path exists, then r = -1.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid). The slice is nonempty, so let n = len(grid[0]). Assume m >= 1, n >= 1, every row of grid has length n, m*n <= 100000, for every i with 0 <= i < m and every j with 0 <= j < n we have 0 <= grid[i][j] < m*n, and grid[m-1][n-1] = 0.
